title: Data Drift vs Concept Drift
interviewAnswer: Data drift means the input distribution changes; concept drift means the relationship between inputs and target changes. Drift detection is a signal to investigate—not automatic proof that retraining is needed.
why: Drift questions test whether you can distinguish changes in inputs from changes in the relationship between inputs and outcomes.
intuition: Data drift means the input distribution changed. Concept drift means the mapping P(y|x) changed, so even familiar inputs may now require different predictions.
deepDive: Covariate/data drift can be detected without labels using distribution comparisons, but it does not automatically imply accuracy loss. Concept/model-performance drift requires labels or strong proxies and can lag in availability. Prior/label shift changes class prevalence. Retraining should be triggered by impact and validated, not every statistical difference.
workedExample: Seasonal customer features shift every December (data drift) while the same fraud rules still work. A new attack pattern that changes which transactions are fraudulent is concept drift.
commonMistakes: Automatically retraining whenever a feature distribution changes slightly.
production: Monitor feature distributions, missingness and model outputs continuously; join delayed ground truth when available and gate retraining with offline evaluation/approval.

visual.title: Distribution drift
visual.caption: Drift means production inputs/predictions differ from the reference distribution; it does not automatically imply worse model quality.
